h1: The 5 Best 80V Leaf Blowers of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: five Greenworks 80V leaf blowers, from 770 CFM handhelds to a 750 CFM backpack, with airflow, price tiers and tradeoffs.
summary: The 770 CFM Greenworks 80V handheld is the best of the group, with the highest listed airflow. The backpack model lists 750 CFM and suits long cleanups. The 730 CFM blower is the value pick, giving up only a little air for a lower price tier. The 700 CFM model is poor value, and the 500 CFM unit is for small patios.
intro: Every blower in this list carries the Greenworks 80V name, which tempts shoppers into assuming they all perform alike. They do not. Listed airflow runs from 500 to 770 CFM, two models cost about half what the others do, and one of them straps to your back instead of living in your hand.

We reviewed five Greenworks 80V blowers and ranked them strictly on the figures in their listings: airflow, format and price tier. The pages do not state battery runtime or air speed, so we left those out of the comparison rather than guess. What remains is a clear question of how much air you need and how much you will pay for it.

products.name: Greenworks 80V Electric Leaf Blower (770 CFM)
products.verdict: The highest listed airflow here at 770 CFM, cordless.
products.description:
This Greenworks 80V cordless handheld lists 770 CFM, the highest airflow of any blower on the page, and sits in the $200 to $500 tier. It runs on the 80V battery platform that Greenworks sells across its yard tools.

It takes first place because no other model lists more air, and it holds a 40 CFM edge over the cheaper 730 CFM unit. The backpack below lists 750, but this one gets there in a handheld body without a harness. The cost of that lead is a higher tier than the value model.

Buy it if your yard is big and leaf fall is heavy. The caveat is the thin spec sheet, since the listing gives no air speed or runtime. Those two details are worth checking before you pay, especially if your cleanups last more than a few minutes.
products.idealFor: Large yards with heavy leaf fall.

products.name: Greenworks 80V Backpack Leaf Blower
products.verdict: A 750 CFM backpack format for longer jobs.
products.description:
The Greenworks 80V backpack blower lists 750 CFM in a backpack format, which moves the weight onto your shoulders instead of your wrist. It sits in the $200 to $500 tier, like the top pick.

It lands second because it trails the 770 CFM handheld by 20 CFM, a gap you are unlikely to notice in the yard. The harness is the real selling point here, since long jobs are far more comfortable when the blower is not hanging from one arm. Against the handhelds below, it costs more and is bulkier to store.

Buy it if you clear a large property and spend a long stretch with the blower running. Skip it if your cleanups are short, because a handheld is easier to grab, lighter overall and cheaper to own.

products.name: Greenworks 80V Electric Leaf Blower (730 CFM)
products.description:
This Greenworks 80V handheld lists 730 CFM from a cordless design and sits in the $100 to $200 tier, a full step below the top two.

Third place reflects a very small compromise. It gives up only 40 CFM to the 770 CFM model while costing noticeably less, which makes it the best airflow per dollar in the group. It beats the 700 CFM unit below on both airflow and price, a combination that makes the other model hard to recommend.

Buy it if you have a big yard and want strong airflow without the top-tier price. The caveat is a thin listing with no air speed or runtime. If you simply want the maximum number and money is not a concern, the 770 CFM model is the better call.
products.idealFor: Value-minded buyers with a big yard.

products.name: Greenworks 80V Electric Leaf Blower (700 CFM)
products.verdict: 700 CFM cordless, but in the higher price tier.
products.description:
The 700 CFM Greenworks 80V handheld is a cordless blower in the $200 to $500 tier. Its format and battery platform match the other handhelds.

It ranks fourth because the numbers do not favor it. The 730 CFM model lists more air and sits in a lower tier, so paying more for 30 CFM less is difficult to justify. Compared with the 770 CFM leader, it saves nothing in price class while giving up 70 CFM. The only advantage is a possible preference for this exact model line.

Buy it if a retailer is clearing it at a discount and you want the 80V platform. Skip it if you are comparing airflow per dollar, because both models around it are better choices. It is not a bad blower, just a poorly positioned one.
products.idealFor: Buyers set on this exact model line.

products.name: Greenworks 80V Electric Leaf Blower (500 CFM)
products.verdict: 500 CFM for small yards in the $100 to $200 tier.
products.description:
This Greenworks 80V handheld lists 500 CFM, the lowest airflow in the ranking, and falls in the $100 to $200 tier. It uses the same 80V battery platform as the larger models.

It lands last because it moves 230 CFM less than the 730 CFM unit while sitting in the same price tier. For a few dollars more you get substantially more air, which makes this a hard model to pick unless the yard is truly small. Its job is patios, driveways and light clean-up rather than lawns buried in leaves.

Buy it if your property is small and leaf fall is modest. Skip it if you face thick piles each autumn. The listing also omits air speed and runtime, so confirm both before ordering if you plan to run it for longer sessions.

whatMatters.detail: CFM measures the volume of air a blower moves each minute, and it sets how quickly piles clear. The models here run from 500 to 770 CFM, a big spread. The figure is usually printed in the listing title, so compare it first, and keep in mind that it is a manufacturer claim.

Format means handheld or backpack. A handheld is light to grab and store, while a backpack puts the weight on your shoulders and suits long jobs. Choose by how long your cleanups run. The Greenworks 80V backpack lists 750 CFM, and the handhelds list the rest. Check the format in the title.

The 80V platform is Greenworks' battery system, and its packs do not fit other brands. That matters because batteries are a big part of the cost. If you already own 80V tools, you may save money. Check whether the listing includes a battery and charger or sells the blower alone.

Price tier groups products by cost range, and similar-looking Greenworks blowers sit in different tiers. The 730 CFM model is in the $100 to $200 tier, while the 700 CFM model is in the $200 to $500 tier. Compare CFM against tier before buying so you do not overpay for less air.

Missing specs are a quiet risk. These listings do not state runtime or air speed, both of which affect real-world use. Read the full listing, the product images and the manual download if available. If those figures are absent, ask the seller or choose a model with clearer documentation.

faq.a: The three handheld models are listed as cordless, and the 80V backpack is identified by its format. All of them use the Greenworks 80V platform, so check whether a battery and charger come in the box before ordering.

Assuming all 80V Greenworks blowers perform alike. Airflow ranges from 500 CFM on the lightest model to 770 CFM on the top handheld, and price tiers differ too, so compare each listing instead of trusting the brand name.

faq.q: Is the 770 CFM worth it over 730 CFM?
faq.a: It depends on your yard. The 770 CFM model adds 40 CFM and costs more than the 730 CFM unit. For a big property with heavy leaf fall the top pick is worth it; otherwise the 730 CFM blower is the better buy.

faq.q: How do I set one up?
faq.a: Charge the 80V battery, attach the nozzle and test the blower on a hard surface before clearing leaves. For the backpack model, adjust the harness so the weight sits on your shoulders and hips, not on your back.
Keep the air intake clear of leaves and debris, wipe the housing after use, and store the battery as directed in the manual. Avoid leaving it in extreme heat or cold, which shortens battery life.
The 500 CFM Greenworks 80V model is the lightest duty. It suits small yards and patios, and it moves 230 CFM less than the 730 CFM blower that costs about the same.

finalTake: The 770 CFM Greenworks 80V handheld is the best blower here for large yards, with the 750 CFM backpack as the comfortable choice for long jobs. For most buyers, the 730 CFM model is the smart value pick, giving up little air for less money. Skip the 700 CFM unit, and keep the 500 CFM blower for patios.
